clips.send: Ozone layer. Earth’s sunscreen, about 15–35 km. A zone inside the stratosphere where ozone gas (O3) is most concentrated. Ozone absorbs most of the Sun’s harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays, protecting living things from sunburn, skin cancer and eye damage. Chemicals called CFCs (once used in spray cans and refrigerators) thinned it, causing the “ozone hole” over Antarctica. A 1987 treaty (the Montreal Protocol) began phasing them out; they are now banned almost everywhere, and the layer is slowly healing.
clips.text: Ozone layer. Earth’s sunscreen, ~15–35 km. A zone inside the stratosphere where ozone gas (O₃) is most concentrated.. Ozone absorbs most of the Sun’s harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays, protecting living things from sunburn, skin cancer and eye damage.. Chemicals called CFCs (once used in spray cans and refrigerators) thinned it, causing the “ozone hole” over Antarctica. A 1987 treaty (the Montreal Protocol) began phasing them out; they are now banned almost everywhere, and the layer is slowly healing.

clips.send: Troposphere. 0–12 km, where weather happens. The lowest layer: about 8 km thick over the poles and 16–18 km thick over the equator. It holds about 75–80 percent of all the air and almost all the water vapor, so nearly all clouds, rain and storms form here. Temperature drops about 6.5 degrees Celsius for every kilometer you climb, because this layer is heated from the ground below. Air here keeps mixing by convection: warm air rises and cool air sinks.

It holds about 75–80% of all the air and almost all the water vapor, so nearly all clouds, rain and storms form here.. clips.send: Mesosphere. 50–85 km, meteors burn up here. The coldest layer: about minus 90 degrees Celsius near its top. Most meteors (“shooting stars”) burn up here as they rub against air molecules at high speed. Too high for planes and balloons, too low for satellites, so it is the least explored layer.

clips.send: Global winds. Uneven heating + Earth’s spin. The Sun heats the equator more than the poles. Warm air rises at the equator and cooler air flows in to replace it, forming giant convection loops. Earth’s rotation bends moving air (the Coriolis effect), so winds blow at an angle instead of straight north–south. Trade winds (0–30°) blow from the east toward the equator; prevailing westerlies (30–60°) blow from the west; polar easterlies (60–90°) blow from the east. The westerlies carry most weather across the United States from west to east.

clips.send: Stratosphere. 12–50 km, calm layered air. Air moves mostly sideways in calm layers with little up-and-down mixing, so the ride is smooth. Temperature RISES with height here, because ozone absorbs ultraviolet (UV) energy from the Sun. Weather balloons rise to about 30–35 km before they burst. Big jets cruise near the bottom of this layer. It contains the ozone layer.

clips.send: Thermosphere. 85–600 km, auroras and the ISS. The air is extremely thin. Its few particles absorb X-rays and UV light and can reach 500–2,000 degrees Celsius . It would not feel hot to you: there are so few particles that very little heat would reach your skin. Auroras (the northern and southern lights) glow here when charged particles from the Sun hit gas atoms. The International Space Station orbits in the thermosphere, about 400 km up. Its lower part (the ionosphere) bounces radio waves around Earth.

clips.send: Exosphere. Above about 600 km, fades into space. The outermost layer, made mostly of very thin hydrogen and helium. Particles are so far apart they rarely collide, and some escape into space. Many satellites orbit here. The layer slowly fades into outer space about 10,000 km up.

clips.send: 热层。85–600 千米 · 极光和国际空间站。空气极其稀薄。少量气体粒子吸收 X 射线和紫外线，温度可达 500–2000 摄氏度 。但你并不会觉得热：粒子太少，传到皮肤上的热量非常少。来自太阳的带电粒子撞击气体原子时，会在这里发出极光。国际空间站在约 400 千米高的热层中运行。热层下部的电离层能反射无线电波，让它绕地球传播。

clips.send: 臭氧层。地球的“防晒霜”，约 15–35 千米。平流层中臭氧（O3）最集中的区域。臭氧吸收了太阳的大部分有害紫外线，保护生物免受晒伤、皮肤癌和眼睛损伤。氟利昂（CFCs，过去用于喷雾罐和冰箱）曾使它变薄，在南极上空形成“臭氧空洞”。1987 年签订的《蒙特利尔议定书》开始逐步淘汰这类物质，如今它们几乎在全世界都已被禁用，臭氧层正在慢慢恢复。
clips.text: 臭氧层. 地球的“防晒霜”，约 15–35 千米. 平流层中臭氧（O₃）最集中的区域。. 臭氧吸收了太阳的大部分有害紫外线，保护生物免受晒伤、皮肤癌和眼睛损伤。. 氟利昂（CFCs，过去用于喷雾罐和冰箱）曾使它变薄，在南极上空形成“臭氧空洞”。1987 年签订的《蒙特利尔议定书》开始逐步淘汰这类物质，如今它们几乎在全世界都已被禁用，臭氧层正在慢慢恢复。

clips.send: 全球风带。不均匀受热 + 地球自转。太阳对赤道的加热比对两极多。赤道的热空气上升，较冷的空气流过来补充，形成巨大的对流环流。地球自转使运动的空气发生偏转（地转偏向力，即科里奥利效应），所以风是斜着吹的，而不是正南正北。信风（0–30 度 ）从东边吹向赤道；盛行西风（30–60 度 ）从西边吹来；极地东风（60–90 度 ）从东边吹来。盛行西风把美国大部分地区的天气从西向东推进。

clips.send: 散逸层（外层）。约 600 千米以上 · 逐渐过渡到太空。最外面的一层，主要是极稀薄的氢和氦。粒子相距很远，很少相互碰撞，有些会逃逸到太空中。许多人造卫星在这里运行。它在大约 10000 千米高处逐渐过渡为太空。

clips.send: 中间层。50–85 千米 · 流星在这里燃烧。最冷的一层：顶部附近约减90 摄氏度 。大多数流星以极高速度与空气分子摩擦，在这里燃烧殆尽。对飞机和气球来说太高，对卫星来说又太低，所以它是人类了解最少的一层。

clips.send: 平流层。12–50 千米 · 平稳的层状大气。空气以水平运动为主，很少上下对流，所以比较平稳。这里的气温随高度升高而升高，因为臭氧吸收了太阳的紫外线。气象气球能升到约 30–35 千米才会胀破；大型客机常在这一层的底部附近巡航。臭氧层就在平流层里。

clips.send: 对流层。0–12 千米 · 天气现象发生在这里。最低的一层：两极上空约 8 千米厚，赤道上空约 16–18 千米厚。它集中了大约 75–百分之80 的空气和几乎全部的水汽，所以云、雨和风暴几乎都在这里形成。每升高 1 千米，气温大约下降 6.5 摄氏度 ，因为这一层主要靠地面加热。这里的空气不断进行对流：热空气上升，冷空气下沉。
